`†` crud/search/reindex ran on an incomplete corpus (import below 1000/1000 bundles or not run before it, or the ES index not drained); on bulk-import and its initial index, search did not return every resource it ingested · `‡` more than 1% errors or failed checks in that suite (on bulk-import and its ingest, any resource not ingested; on its initial index, a rebuild that did not complete or reported errors; on reindex, any reindex error or a failed job) · `⚠` contended host (postgres crud above 3 ms/call) or a backend container died · **bold** = best in its row, shown only when no leg in that row carries a marker or `(partial)` (on the bulk-import ingest and initial index rows, also only when every leg indexed the same way) · bulk-import is resources/s through `$bulk-submit` into a fresh database, kick-off until the search index covers it, and its ingest and initial index rows split that time (see the note below the tables); reindex is resources/s of one `$reindex` of the type its row names, in the corpus import loaded, `(partial)` when it did not finish (the reason is in that leg's job summary); each is one asynchronous job, so its p95 is n/a · n/a = no result (reason in brackets)

Import row: **resources/s** = entries of the transaction Bundles that committed (k6 `bundle_size`) per second of the import scenario's own clock, which starts after k6 setup() has loaded the two seed Bundles (that time is in Leg health) — the unit upstream's report uses. Its p95 is **per Bundle**: one k6 iteration, the corpus fetch plus the transaction POST. k6's `http_reqs` is not used for import: it counts a corpus GET beside every Bundle POST. Bundles/s is in Leg health.

Bulk-import ingest and initial index rows: the same `$bulk-submit` load as the `bulk-import` row, split into the two times a user waits for. **Ingest** = resources ingested ÷ seconds from kick-off until the status manifest is final, those seconds in brackets: how long loading the corpus takes. **Initial index** = seconds from then until HFS's deferred search-index rebuild of that freshly loaded data has finished (HFS_BULK_SUBMIT_DEFER_INDEXING, the default); the Search check in the Bulk import table then confirms it is searchable. `inline (during ingest)` = the backend indexed each batch while ingesting (DEFER_INDEXING=false), so its indexing time is inside its ingest seconds — it is not a zero-second index; `+ N s rebuild` is a follow-up rebuild of the types the index rejected. No best is marked on either row when legs indexed differently. Both rows are in the Throughput table only (one asynchronous job: no p95; failed resources are in the bulk-import Errors row).

### Bulk import (`$bulk-submit`)

Each leg loaded the corpus `import` loads (its 2 seed bundles and 1,000 bundles, converted to per-resource-type NDJSON) through `$bulk-submit`, in a fresh database served by a second HFS, after the search suite. **Ingest** is kick-off until the status manifest is final; **Index** is the deferred search-index rebuild that follows (followed in the second HFS's log); **Total** is both, and is what the `bulk-import` row above divides the ingested resources by; the ingest and initial index rows above show **Ingest** and **Index** on their own. **Index** reads `inline (during ingest)` when HFS indexed while ingesting, so that time is inside **Ingest**. **Search check** compares Patient and Observation totals and two indexed queries with the converted corpus. It counts the 3,349 seed resources the `import` row's entries do not.

| Leg | Result | Resources ingested | Ingest | Index | Total | Search check |
